name: Christian mysticism
scope: Christian mysticism as the scholarship (Turner, Inge, Underhill, Scott) uses the name: the tradition of Christian writers on the soul's ascent to and union with God, running from the Church Fathers and Pseudo-Dionysius through the mediaeval apophatic and cataphatic mystics (Eckhart, Tauler, Suso, the Cloud author, Julian, Bonaventure, Bernard) to Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross. It includes the Eastern Orthodox theoria strand named by the redirects. It is a body of spiritual and theological teaching, so the audit answers only what those sources state it holds; it excludes the occult 'Mystic Christianity' of Heindel, Ramacharaka and the Order of Christian Mystics (theosophical and Rosicrucian teachings the scholarship does not tie to the tradition), Huxley's secular religion, and the ideas of any one author or church outside the key works and figures named.

summary: Christian mysticism is the tradition of Christian teaching on the soul's journey into God, through purgation, illumination and union, set out by writers from Pseudo-Dionysius and Augustine to Eckhart, Julian, Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross. Its sources are spiritual and theological, so they speak to politics very little; the one test-statement position they state is that the seeker must detach from desire for worldly things.
